First Bail Application under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (erstwhile Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973) has been filed on behalf of the Applicant, Uma Lamba for grant of Anticipatory Bail and release on Bail in the event of arrest in FIR No. 0705/2024 under Section 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 85/316/3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, dated 03.12.2024 registered at Police Station Palam Village, District South-West.
2.

sentences.text: 3. Pankaj Lamba and Harshita Barela got married on 22.03.2024 according to Hindu rights and ceremonies, in an arranged marriage.

It was alleged by the Complainant that the co-accused and his family had subjected the Complainant's daughter and her family to cruelty and harassment connected to dowry demand, even prior to the solemnisation of their marriage.
4.
After the marriage, the co-accused Pankaj Lamba (husband) went to United Kingdom, while the Complainant's daughter moved into her matrimonial home in Dharoli.
She was allegedly subjected to harassment and cruelty, which led her to leave the matrimonial home and stay at her parental house.
She later moved to Corby City, United Kingdom, on 30.04.2024, where the cruelty persisted until her death on 14.11.2024.

The Complainant was informed about her death on 15.11.2024.
5.

The Complainant is the father of the deceased who has alleged that his daughter was subjected to cruelty or harassment by the Applicant and her husband and on whose complaint, FIR under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC was registered and thereafter, Section 304B was added.
6.
Learned Senior Counsel for the Applicant has submitted that the Applicant is in judicial custody since 14.03.2025.

The prosecution has wrongly added Section 304B as at the relevant time, the Applicant had no nexus with the Complainant's daughter as she was residing in UK and thus, it is wrong to allege that she was subject to any kind of cruelty or harassment for or in relation to the dowry demand by the Applicant.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 29/06/2025 at 23:43:27 7.

Learned Senior Counsel submitted that the learned Sessions' Court has erroneously dismissed Applicant's bail Application vide Order dated 01.04.2025 and did not consider that the FIR does not disclose any allegation of cruelty or harassment "soon before death" which resulted into the dowry death of the deceased and therefore, the Applicant has approached this Court for bail.
8.

It is also submitted that this Court vide Order dated 04.04.2025 and Order dated 08.04.2025 has granted interim protection to Satinder Kumar, brother-in-law of the Applicant and Lalita, sister of the Applicant.
Also, vide Order dated 09.04.2025, Uma Lamba, daughter of the Applicant has also been granted anticipatory bail.

Reliance has been placed on Pepsi Foods Ltd. Vs. Special Judicial Magistrate (1998) 5 SCC 749 to submit that at the time of consideration of grant of bail, the Court has to take a prima facie view whether offence has been made out or not.

9. Reliance has been placed on the case of Manohar Lal vs. State of Haryana, (2014) 9 SCC 645 wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that "Facts must show existence of proximate live link between the effect of cruelty based on dowry demand and death of victim".
10.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

Reliance has also been placed Balwant Singh and Anr. vs. State of Punjab, (2004) 7 SCC 724, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that since one of the ingredients of the offence under Section 304B IPC Sunil Devi vs State Of Nct Of Delhi on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140872606/
2 is that cruelty should have been meted out to the deceased soon before her death, it is for the prosecution to establish affirmatively that the victim was subjected to cruelty and harassment based on dowry demand soon before her death.
11.

12. Furthermore, the grant of Bail is a norm and refusal thereof is exception and the Courts should exercise the discretion of Bail judicially and the Bail should not be denied to an accused only as a punishment.
13. Thus, it is prayed that Bail be granted to the Applicant.

14. In the Status Report filed on behalf of the State it is stated that the Complainant in his complaint has mentioned that his daughter had many times complained that her husband and in-laws are not good people and they may kill her for want of money.
It is also mentioned that an amount of Rs.15,00,000/- was given to the family of Pankaj Lamba for visa of UK in September, 2024.
The deceased filed a Domestic Violence Complaint against her husband, Mr. Pankaj Lamba, for beating for dowry demands.
15. It was further stated that on 10.11.2024 at 10:00 p.m, his daughter made a video call to him wherein she was continuously crying and was saying that she be taken away or her husband may kill her.
Sister-in-law, Ms. Uma also used to threaten her on phone call from India.

16. The Statement of the parents of the deceased, namely, Smt. Sudesh and Complainant, Mr. Satbir Singh, were recorded by the SDM on 30.11.2024 wherein they sated that dowry demands of huge cash and jewellery was being made by the husband and his relatives from the deceased since the date of her marriage and she was being regularly harassed and tortured on this account.
She was also threatened that in case, the demands were not fulfilled, she would have to bear the consequences.
17. The Bail Application was opposed on the grounds that there were specific allegations against the Applicant for demand of dowry and This is a digitally signed order.

The investigation is at an initial stage and there is an apprehension of tampering with the evidence and this Application deserves to be dismissed.
18. It is submitted that the Bail Application is liable to be dismissed.

sentences.text: Submissions heard and record perused.

20. The allegation against the Applicant/mother-in-law is that at the time marriage of deceased was fixed with her son, demand of Rs.5,00,000/- was made and the deceased was harassed for not bringing this even after the marriage.
The fact remains that marriage between Applicant's son/Pankaj Lamba with the deceased was solemnized on 22.03.2024.
The deceased had joined her husband in UK where she picked up a job and the unfortunate incident of her demise also took place in UK.
She died on 14.11.2024 and investigation in the present FIR is in progress, which is likely to take time.

21. It is to be noted that the deceased had stayed at her matrimonial house only for about 10-15 days,
after which she moved to her Parental home and from there she went to the UK.
The alleged dowry death occurred in the UK and the Applicant was here in India and as such no specific role as been ascribed to the Applicant.

23. With aforesaid, the present Bail Application is accordingly disposed of.
